completebead_disposition_judgment: ACCEPTED as the right call, with one condition for the tally. I verified both factual claims rather than trusting them: (a) internal/complete/complete.go:1099 is the SOLE production CompleteBead call site and passes msg="" unconditionally, so the `if msg != ""` auto-commit branch at mindspec_executor.go:~364-380 is genuinely unreachable from production since bead 6 moved materialization into runMaterialization; (b) the surrounding comments make NO false mechanism claim — they accurately describe the function's own contract ('Auto-commit if message provided ... When msg is empty the caller is responsible'), and commitWithExport genuinely still serves its other live call sites. Given that, deferral over in-dispatch surgery is correct on three grounds: removing the branch means changing CompleteBead's Executor-interface signature (rippling through the interface, MindspecExecutor, MockExecutor, and every test decorator wrapping CompleteBead — including this bead's own fixture executors), CompleteBead is the single most sensitive shared mutation function in the executor, and a doc-precision round is the wrong vehicle for an interface change. Unlike residualDirtyPaths (standalone, zero-reference, delete-in-place), this is a live-signatured dead branch. CONDITION: a commit-message observation is not a durable disposition in this project — the follow-up must land as a tracked bd issue before the spec's impl-approve, so it cannot evaporate the way un-consolidated riders did in this panel's own round 1. Filing it is an orchestration action for the tally/orchestrator, not a code change, so it does not hold my verdict.
